drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A U S health insurer runs everything on A W S
drills.answer_line: SAM: So the answer is C, Bedrock.
drills.stem: An AWS-only health insurer with a large AWS commitment wants Claude to summarise claims files with patient data. Compliance says the workload must stay inside the AWS boundary under its HIPAA programme. Which route fits?

options.A: The Claude API direct, with US-only inference
options.B: Claude Platform on AWS, billed through AWS Marketplace
options.D: Claude in Microsoft Foundry, Hosted on Azure

drills.why: Bedrock is AWS-operated with no Anthropic operator access, Anthropic's docs point HIPAA workloads there, and spend lands on the AWS commit. B is Anthropic-operated, processes data outside the AWS boundary and is not HIPAA-ready. A misses boundary and bill. D draws down Azure's commitment.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false. One: on Bedrock
drills.answer_line: SAM: Four out of five. Four is true: the partner sets the lifecycle.
drills.prompt: True or false? 1) On Bedrock, Anthropic staff can operate the serving infrastructure. 2) Signing up for Claude Platform on AWS converts your existing Anthropic org in place. 3) A private-offer discount agreed for Bedrock carries over to Claude Platform on AWS. 4) A model retired on the Claude API can still be served on Bedrock. 5) Prompt caching works on Bedrock.
drills.answer: 1) False: AWS operates it, no Anthropic operator access. 2) False: it creates a new org. 3) False: private offers do not transfer. 4) True: the partner sets the lifecycle. 5) True.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A manufacturer runs on Azure
drills.answer_line: SAM: A is right. C is the near miss
drills.stem: Choose two. A manufacturer on Azure with a large MACC requires prompts and completions to stay in Azure. Which two statements are true?

options.A: Foundry Hosted on Azure keeps prompts and completions in Azure
options.B: Foundry spend draws down the MACC under either hosting option
options.C: The Message Batches API is available on Hosted on Anthropic
options.D: Claude Platform on AWS spend also counts against the MACC, since both bill in CCU
options.E: Hosted on Azure supports Agent Skills and the Files API

drills.why: Hosted on Azure keeps prompts in Azure; both Foundry options are MACC-eligible. Batches is on neither Foundry option, CCU billed by another cloud does not decrement the MACC, and Skills and Files return an error on Hosted on Azure.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A retailer has a large Google Cloud commitment
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. Anthropic operates it, so Managed Agents and Skills are there
drills.stem: A retailer with a large Google Cloud commitment wants a returns agent on Claude Managed Agents with Agent Skills, with all spend on the Google Cloud bill. Which route?

options.B: The Anthropic-managed Claude offer on Google Cloud Marketplace
options.C: The Claude API direct, with a separate Anthropic invoice
options.D: Gemini Enterprise with Claude Opus switched on for staff

drills.why: Anthropic-managed carries Managed Agents and Skills and draws down the Google commit. A lacks both features, C misses the bill, D is an employee product whose seat credits cover Gemini only.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A logistics company on A W S
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. Two frameworks, two labs
drills.stem: A logistics company on AWS runs LangGraph and Strands agents calling Claude and OpenAI models on Bedrock. It wants one managed runtime with agent identity, a gateway exposing Lambda functions as MCP tools, and a policy layer, on the AWS bill. What fits?
drills.why: AgentCore is framework- and model-agnostic, with Gateway, Identity and Policy. Managed Agents runs Anthropic's harness for Claude; Agents Classic is reportedly closed to new customers; Kiro is a coding agent.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the five segments
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Two questions, the A W S doors, Google and Azure
drills.prompt: Name the five segments, and the question you would ask the customer in each.
drills.answer: Two questions; the AWS doors; Google and Azure; the table; AWS's own stack. Who operates and who bills; boundary or platform; which commitment; which region; one lab or several.

In this episode: Clouds both resell Claude and compete with Anthropic's platform
One table: operator, features, residency, commitment
Two doors each on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure
AWS's own stack: Nova, AgentCore, Strands, Kiro
Cold open: the health insurer: Seven doors to Claude, counting hosting options
Read the constraint: boundary, bill or features
Segment one: two questions: Who operates it: decides features and data processor
Whose bill: decides which commitment it burns
Cloud-operated: model plus core Messages features
Anthropic-operated marketplace: most of the platform; Anthropic processes data
Source: Anthropic's own docs list each door's gaps
OpenAI on Bedrock, Claude in Foundry: the cloud picks the door, not the lab
Segment two: the A W S doors: Bedrock: AWS-operated, two endpoints, check model per endpoint
Bedrock: FedRAMP High, IL4/5, HIPAA; native IAM and quotas
Bedrock lacks Files, Skills, server tools, Batches API, Managed Agents
Claude Platform on AWS: Anthropic-operated, near-full platform, billed in CCU
Platform gaps: not HIPAA-ready, no fast mode, ZDR opt-in
Commit drawdown for Platform: get AWS's wording
Segment three: Google Cloud and Azure: Google-managed: Model Garden on Agent Platform (ex-Vertex AI)
Anthropic-managed Google: Skills, batch, Files, Managed Agents
Foundry: two hosting options, Anthropic operates both
Neither Foundry option has Managed Agents or Compliance API
CSP-resold Azure subscriptions cannot buy Claude
Foundry: Anthropic is data processor; in M365 Copilot, a subprocessor
Segment four: the table in your head: Columns: operator, features, residency and compliance, commitment
Rows: direct, cloud-operated, Anthropic-operated marketplace, Azure
EU residency differs per door and per model
Google single-region endpoints: older models only
Model lag small; feature lag structural
Segment five: A W S's own stack: Nova 2: Lite, Pro, Sonic, Omni; Forge; Act priced per agent-hour
AgentCore: managed services incl. Runtime, Gateway, Identity, Policy
Managed Agents: Anthropic's harness for Claude
Strands: Apache 2.0, Python and TypeScript, MCP and A2A
Kiro: spec-driven, IDE and CLI; Q Developer IDE support ends 30 Apr 2027
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: C, Claude in Amazon Bedrock
Claude Platform on AWS: outside AWS boundary, not HIPAA-ready
Tell: "must stay inside the AWS boundary"
Five to remember: Operator decides features and processor; bill decides commitment
Cloud-run doors: core model inside the cloud boundary, no server-side platform
Anthropic-run marketplace doors: nearly full platform on the cloud bill
Foundry: MACC either way, no Managed Agents or Batches
AWS competes on the agent stack: AgentCore, Strands, Kiro, Nova
Recap: conversation tells: "We're an AWS shop" → boundary (Bedrock) or Managed Agents (Platform)?
HIPAA or FedRAMP High → cloud-operated door first
Accepted the Vertex gap → Anthropic-managed Google carries the platform
Managed Agents or batch on the MACC → Foundry has neither today
Several frameworks and labs on AWS → AgentCore before Managed Agents
Leaving Q Developer → Kiro by default; argue Claude Code on the harness
